lesson.title: Code Your Own CLI With Rust
lesson.goal: build a command-line tool in Rust with cargo that parses arguments

sources.title: Code Your Own CLI With Rust

steps.title: Create Cargo project and add clap
steps.instructions: Run `cargo new bestls` (or your own name) and cd into it. Add `clap` with the `derive` feature under [dependencies] in Cargo.toml.

targets.caption: Add clap with the derive feature under [dependencies]

explanations.topic: Using clap derive feature for CLI parsing

hints: Use `cargo new` to scaffold a binary Rust project in an empty folder.
common_mistakes: Forgetting to enable the `derive` feature on `clap`, which prevents `#[derive(Parser)]` from working.
Adding `clap` before running `cd bestls` inside the new project directory.

steps.title: Define CLI struct and parse arguments
steps.instructions: In src/main.rs define a struct deriving `Debug` and `Parser` with an optional `PathBuf` field `path`, call `parse()` in main. Run `cargo run -- -h`.

targets.caption: Define the CLI struct with an optional PathBuf argument

explanations.topic: Passing flags after `--` in cargo run
How clap generates help output from the struct

hints: Import `clap::Parser` and `std::path::PathBuf` at the top of `src/main.rs`.
Make `path` an `Option<PathBuf>` so the directory argument is optional.
common_mistakes: Running `cargo run -h` instead of `cargo run -- -h`, which shows Cargo's own help instead of your CLI's.
Forgetting to import `clap::Parser` in `src/main.rs`.
steps.code: use clap::Parser; use std::path::PathBuf; #[derive(Debug, Parser)] struct CLI { path: Option<PathBuf>, } fn main() { let cli = CLI::parse(); println!("Hello, world!"); }

steps.title: Add command version and about metadata
steps.instructions: Add `#[command(version, about, long_about = "...")]` above your CLI struct in src/main.rs. Run `cargo run -- --version` and `cargo run -- --help`.

targets.caption: Add version, about, and long_about attributes

explanations.topic: Auto-generating --version and long help text via #[command]

hints: Place `#[command(...)]` directly under `#[derive(Debug, Parser)]` on `struct CLI`.
Include `version, about, long_about = "Best Ls command ever"` inside `#[command(...)]`.
Run `cargo run -- --help` to see both the description and `-V, --version`.
common_mistakes: Misspelling `long_about` or omitting quotes around the description string.
Testing `-v` (lowercase) instead of `-V` or `--version`.
steps.code: #[derive(Debug, Parser)] #[command(version, about, long_about = "Best Ls command ever")] struct CLI { path: Option<PathBuf>, }

steps.title: Unwrap optional path with default
steps.instructions: In `main`, unwrap `cli.path` with `unwrap_or(PathBuf::from("."))` and print `path.display()`. Run `cargo run -- longpath` and then `cargo run` to verify both paths.

targets.caption: Default to the current directory when no path argument is supplied

explanations.topic: Defaulting the optional path argument to `.`

hints: Because `cli.path` is an `Option<PathBuf>`, call `.unwrap_or(...)` on it.
common_mistakes: Trying to print `PathBuf` directly with `{}` instead of `path.display()`.
Passing `"."` as a `&str` directly to `unwrap_or` instead of wrapping it in `PathBuf::from(".")`.

steps.title: Check path existence with colored errors
steps.instructions: Add owo-colors = "4.2.1" to Cargo.toml and import fs and OwoColorize in src/main.rs. Check fs::exists(&path) and print a red error when the path does not exist or cannot be read.

targets.caption: Verify the target path exists and handle missing or unreadable paths

explanations.topic: Why fs::exists returns Result<bool> instead of bool

hints: Use `if let Ok(does_exist) = fs::exists(&path)` to handle both the `Result` and the boolean.
Call `.red()` on the error string literals inside `println!("{}", ...)`.
common_mistakes: Forgetting to import `owo_colors::OwoColorize`, which causes `.red()` not to be found.
Passing `path` by value instead of `&path` to `fs::exists`, moving `path` before later use.
steps.code: use owo_colors::OwoColorize; use std::{fs, path::PathBuf}; if let Ok(does_exist) = fs::exists(&path) { if does_exist { } else { println!("{}", "Path does not exist".red()); } } else { println!("{}", "error reading directory".red()); }

steps.title: Read directory entries in get_files
steps.instructions: Create `fn get_files(path: &Path) -> Vec<String>` that collects entry names with `fs::read_dir`. Loop over `get_files(&path)` inside the exists branch, print each name, and run `cargo run`.

targets.caption: Implement get_files to read directory entries into a Vec<String>

explanations.topic: Converting OsString from file_name() into String

hints: Initialize `let mut data = Vec::default();` and push `file.file_name().into_string().unwrap_or("unknown name".into())`.
Loop over `get_files(&path)` in `main` when `does_exist` is true.
common_mistakes: Forgetting to import `std::path::Path` alongside `PathBuf`.
Leaving a semicolon after `data` at the end of `get_files`, causing a return-type mismatch.
steps.code: for file in get_files(&path) { println!("{}", file); } fn get_files(path: &Path) -> Vec<String> { let mut data = Vec::default(); if let Ok(read_dir) = fs::read_dir(path) { for entry in read_dir { if let Ok(file) = entry { data.push(file.file_name().into_string().unwrap_or("unknown name".into())); } } } data }

steps.title: Collect file metadata into FileEntry
steps.instructions: Add `strum` and `strum_macros` (0.27) to `Cargo.toml`, define `EntryType` and `FileEntry`, and make `get_files` return `Vec<FileEntry>`. Build each entry in `map_data` using `fs::metadata(&file.path())`, then run `cargo run`.

targets.caption: Define FileEntry and EntryType to hold file metadata
Read metadata for each entry path rather than the parent directory

explanations.topic: Using strum::Display for enum string formatting

common_mistakes: Passing `&path` instead of `&file.path()` to `fs::metadata`, which reports the directory's metadata for every file.
Forgetting to change the return type of `get_files` from `Vec<String>` to `Vec<FileEntry>`.
steps.code: #[derive(Debug, Display)] enum EntryType { File, Dir, } #[derive(Debug)] struct FileEntry { name: String, e_type: EntryType, len_btyes: u64, modified: String, } fn map_data(file: fs::DirEntry, data: &mut Vec<FileEntry>) { if let Ok(meta) = fs::metadata(&file.path()) { data.push(FileEntry { name: file.file_name().into_string().unwrap_or("unknown name".into()), e_type: if meta.is_dir() { EntryType::Dir } else { EntryType::File }, len_btyes: meta.len(), modified: "".to_string(), }); } }

steps.title: Format and color output with tabled
steps.instructions: Add tabled = "0.20.0" to Cargo.toml and derive Tabled on FileEntry with #[tabled(rename = ...)] headers. Build a Table::new(...) with Style::rounded() and column/row colors, then cargo run.

targets.caption: Create and style the table using tabled

explanations.topic: Customizing table borders and column colors with tabled

common_mistakes: Importing `Style` from `owo_colors` instead of `tabled::settings::Style`.
Declaring `let table = ...` without `mut`, which prevents calling `table.with(...)` and `table.modify(...)`.
steps.code: #[derive(Debug, Tabled)] struct FileEntry { #[tabled(rename = "Name")] name: String, #[tabled(rename = "Type")] e_type: EntryType, #[tabled(rename = "Size B")] len_btyes: u64, modified: String, } let get_files = get_files(&path); let mut table = Table::new(get_files); table.with(Style::rounded()); table.modify(Columns::first(), Color::FG_BRIGHT_CYAN); table.modify(Columns::one(2), Color::FG_BRIGHT_MAGENTA); table.modify(Columns::one(3), Color::FG_BRIGHT_MAGENTA); table.modify(Rows::first(), Color::FG_BRIGHT_GREEN); println!("{}", table);

steps.title: Format modified timestamps with chrono
steps.instructions: Add `chrono = "0.4.41"` to `Cargo.toml` and convert `meta.modified()` into `DateTime<Utc>` in `map_data`, formatting it as a date. Set column 3's color to `Color::FG_BRIGHT_YELLOW` and run `cargo run -- src`.

targets.caption: Convert SystemTime to DateTime<Utc> and format it

hints: Avoid naming the variable `mod` since it is a Rust keyword (use `modi`).
common_mistakes: Using `mod` as a binding name in `if let Ok(mod) = ...`, which causes a syntax error in Rust.
Forgetting the type annotation `let date: DateTime<Utc> = modi.into();`.
steps.code: modified: if let Ok(modi) = meta.modified() { let date: DateTime<Utc> = modi.into(); format!("{}", date.format("%a %b %e %Y")) } else { String::default() }

steps.title: Add JSON output flag with serde
steps.instructions: Add serde (with derive) and serde_json to Cargo.toml and derive Serialize on EntryType and FileEntry. Add #[arg(short, long)] json: bool to the CLI struct and print serde_json::to_string output when cli.json is set.

targets.caption: Add the -j / --json boolean flag to the CLI struct
Serialize the FileEntry list to JSON when the flag is set

explanations.topic: Adding short and long boolean flags with #[arg(short, long)]
Serializing nested structs and enums with serde::Serialize

hints: Place `#[arg(short, long)]` above `json: bool` so clap treats it as `-j` / `--json` instead of a positional argument.
common_mistakes: Omitting `#[arg(short, long)]` on `json: bool`, which causes clap to panic because positional bool arguments require an action.
Deriving `Serialize` on `FileEntry` without also deriving `Serialize` on `EntryType`.
steps.code: #[derive(Debug, Parser)] #[command(version, about, long_about = "Best Ls command ever")] struct CLI { path: Option<PathBuf>, #[arg(short, long)] json: bool, } if cli.json { let get_files = get_files(&path); println!("{}", serde_json::to_string(&get_files).unwrap_or("cannot parse json".to_string())); } else { print_table(path); }
